quote.translation: That this so-called third Critique, as the crown of the system of critical philosophy that unifies and completes Kant's world-view, has given great influence both to the Romantic philosophy immediately after Kant and to the idealist philosophy of the present day is not by chance" (Tanabe Hajime, Kanto no mokuteki ron, pp. 2-3 ).

regions.text: x）。「盲人の不自由な境涯を出來るだけ體驗しょうとして時には盲人を美むかの知くであつた彼が後年ほんたうの盲人になつたのは實に少年時代からのさういふ心がけが影響してるるので、思へば優然でないのである』（谷N調一処衣祭め、二七買）。

quote.translation: Or again: "That he, who, trying to experience as far as he could the unfree condition of the blind, sometimes seemed almost to envy the blind, became in later years truly blind, is in fact because such an attitude of mind since his boyhood had its influence, and when one thinks of it, it is not by chance" (Tanizaki Jun'ichirō, Shunkinshō, p. 27).

regions.text: これらは、「偶然でない」の代りに「必然である」を置き換へることが出来るのですなはち偶然性の立場から、必然性を規定してゐるのである。

quote.translation: In both passages "is necessary" can be put in place of "is not by chance", and so they determine necessity from the standpoint of contingency.

regions.text: また『此附近に工場がないの忠們然でおか」と云ふ場合「工場があることも那榔でおぷ」ことを意味してゐるのであるから偶然性の立場から可能性を規定してゐるのである。

quote.translation: When we say "That there are no factories in this neighbourhood is by chance", we mean "It is also possible that there should be factories", and so we determine possibility from the standpoint of contingency.

regions.text: また「學術研究所の設備が我個では不足してゐるから、知識階級の失菜者間題が解決されないのお働然ではない「と云ふ場合「解決されることは不那撒でおぷ」ことを意味してるるから偶然性の立場から不可能性を規定してのるのであろ。

quote.translation: And when we say "Since facilities for scholarly research institutes are insufficient in our country, it is not by chance that the problem of unemployment among the intellectual class is not solved", we mean "That it should be solved is impossible", and so we determine impossibility from the standpoint of contingency.
